title: When Lexical Change Misleads: Rethinking Dynamic Topic Model Evaluation with Traditional and LLM-Based Metrics
task: Validating temporal coherence and LLM semantic similarity against human judgements
problem: Temporal coherence penalises vocabulary change even when a topic's meaning persists over time.
architecture: 120 topic trajectories (20 per model-dataset pair) shown at three time points; three annotators answer five 5-point questions (1,800 judgements); traditional temporal topic coherence vs human coherence, and GPT-5.5 semantic similarity of beginning and ending themes vs human semantic similarity; topics stratified into Low, Medium and High lexical change; Spearman rho.
metrics: Spearman rho between metric and human ratings
key_results: Traditional temporal coherence vs humans ranges from rho = -0.256 (CoNTM, NYT) to 0.614 (DLDA, DBLP).
LLM semantic similarity agrees with humans for CoNTM (rho 0.609 NYT, 0.721 DBLP, 0.502 arXiv) but not for DLDA (-0.086 DBLP, -0.190 arXiv).
CoNTM-NYT, low lexical change: coherence rho = -0.786 while the LLM score gives 0.801.
strengths: Shows that aggregate metric-human correlations hide opposite behaviour across lexical-change strata.
Recommends reporting lexical and semantic measures together.

limitations.text: Only 120 topics, two models, three English datasets; strata hold six or seven topics, so correlations are sensitive to outliers.
Single LLM configuration; the two metrics are validated against different human questions, so they cannot be ranked directly.
